summary: MarsGIS frontend is a single-page React + TypeScript + Vite app whose primary product is one persistent, full-viewport CesiumJS globe rendered as the Mars body. The "4 screens" are not route-swapped pages — the globe mounts once and never unmounts; the screens are workspace MODES (explore / observations / analysis / results) realized as collapsible dock panels over the canvas. A left dock holds the Layer explorer (mode 1) and Data catalogue (mode 2); a right dock holds the Analysis workspace (mode 3), Results & exports and the Pixel/Spectrum inspector (mode 4). State is a single typed Zustand store split into slices (view, layer, catalog, analysis, result, inspector, gazetteer) with immer for ergonomic nested updates and persist for camera/basemap/panel prefs. A framework-agnostic LayerManager class owns the Cesium ImageryLayerCollection and entity DataSources and reconciles one-way from the store (store -> Cesium, UI never touches Cesium directly), supporting six layer types (basemap/context/geology/footprints/result/quality). CRISM footprints render as clickable polygon entities keyed by observation id; analysis result rasters overlay via the backend's XYZ tile endpoint (UrlTemplateImageryProvider on a GeographicTilingScheme) or a SingleTile provider for small bboxes, with a data-driven legend. A debounced gazetteer search box flies the camera to planetary features (seeded with Nili Fossae). Clicking a result pixel pulls its spectrum + spectral angle from the backend and plots it against the MICA reference with uPlot, always labelling results as candidate matches, never confirmed deposits. The typed API client is generated from the backend's OpenAPI doc (openapi-typescript) plus a hand-written fetch wrapper, with zod validation on the few network payloads the globe depends on. Cesium is configured for Mars by setting Ellipsoid.default to Mars radii before the Viewer is created, using a GeographicTilingScheme that matches the verified NASA Trek 2x1 equirectangular grid, and disabling all Earth-specific chrome (atmosphere, Earth geocoder, base layer picker). The stack is deliberately pinned to the mature Vite 7 + plugin-react 5 + TypeScript 5.9 line rather than the bleeding-edge Vite 8 / plugin-react 6 (Rolldown/oxc) / TypeScript 7 line, because production reliability and typescript-eslint support matter more than being on the newest major. A VITE_USE_MOCKS path backed by tiny bundled sample GeoJSON/JSON lets the pipeline, tests and a smoke run work fully offline for CI.

decisions.choice: Raw, imperative CesiumJS wrapped in ONE persistent React component (GlobeView) that owns the Viewer for its lifetime; a LayerManager class reconciles Cesium state one-way from the Zustand store. Not resium.
decisions.rationale: Cesium's API is imperative and GIS-heavy here (custom Mars ellipsoid, dynamic imagery providers, entity picking, requestRenderMode performance). A single owner + one-way reconciliation (store is the source of truth, store.subscribe pushes into Cesium) is far more robust and debuggable than threading every ImageryLayer/Entity through a declarative React tree. The globe must also survive mode changes without remount, which a persistent imperative component guarantees.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: resium 1.27 (declarative Cesium-in-JSX): adds a dependency that must track both Cesium 1.x and React, re-introduces reconciliation we would fight for dynamic layers and picking, and risks remount/flicker of the globe on mode switches.

decisions.choice: Zustand 5 as a single store composed of typed slices (view/layer/catalog/analysis/result/inspector/gazetteer), with immer middleware for nested updates and persist middleware (partialized to camera, basemapId, panels).
decisions.rationale: Zustand gives selector-based subscriptions outside React (store.subscribe) which LayerManager needs to drive Cesium without re-rendering the whole app; immer keeps slice reducers readable for nested layer/filter state; persist restores the user's last camera/basemap/panel layout. The task explicitly recommended Zustand.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Redux Toolkit (heavier boilerplate, no gain here); React Context + useReducer (no out-of-React subscription, forces re-renders that would stutter the globe); Jotai (atom sprawl for this many cross-cutting fields).

decisions.choice: Persistent single globe canvas; the 4 screens are workspace MODES (dock panel configurations), not separate routed pages. URL state (mode, selected obs, active result, camera) synced manually via the History API in a useUrlSync hook; no react-router.
decisions.rationale: Keeping the Viewer mounted once avoids WebGL context teardown/rebuild and preserves camera continuity between screens — the single most important UX property of a map product. Deep-linking is still supported via query params without pulling in a router whose <Routes> would unmount the globe.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: react-router with page-per-screen (would unmount/remount the Cesium canvas or force an awkward globe-outside-Routes layout); full SPA page swaps (lose camera + layer state between screens).

decisions.choice: Pin Vite 7.3.7 + @vitejs/plugin-react 5.2.0 + TypeScript 5.9.3 + Vitest 3.2.7, NOT Vite 8 / plugin-react 6 / TypeScript 7.
decisions.rationale: Verified that @vitejs/plugin-react 5.2.0 already supports Vite ^8 but uses the mature Babel/esbuild transform, whereas plugin-react 6 pulls the still-stabilizing Rolldown/oxc stack. Verified typescript-eslint 8.71 requires TypeScript <6.1.0, so TypeScript 7 (the native/Go compiler) would break linting. A capstone that must reliably RUN benefits more from the battle-tested line; Node 26.5 satisfies both.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Vite 8.3.4 + plugin-react 6.1.2 (Rolldown + optional oxc-transform/react-compiler peers, bleeding edge); TypeScript 7.0.2 native (no typescript-eslint support, immature ecosystem tooling).

decisions.choice: Configure Cesium for Mars by setting Ellipsoid.default = new Ellipsoid(3396190, 3396190, 3376200) in main.tsx BEFORE any Viewer is created, use GeographicTilingScheme (2 cols x 1 row at level 0) for all imagery, and disable Earth chrome (baseLayerPicker, geocoder, skyAtmosphere, ground atmosphere, sun/moon).
decisions.rationale: Ellipsoid.default is the supported global hook (Cesium >=1.106) and must be set pre-construction so cameras, picking and providers all use Mars radii (equatorial 3,396,190 m / polar 3,376,200 m). GeographicTilingScheme's default 2x1 level-0 layout exactly matches the verified NASA Trek EQ equirectangular grid, so {z}/{y}/{x} maps directly.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Leaving WGS84 and scaling (breaks real coordinates/altitudes); per-provider ad-hoc ellipsoids (inconsistent picking/camera); WebMercatorTilingScheme (wrong projection for Trek EQ global tiles).

decisions.choice: uPlot 1.6.32 (framework-agnostic, wrapped in a thin SpectrumChart.tsx) for spectral-angle / reflectance-vs-wavelength plots.
decisions.rationale: CRISM spectra are hundreds of wavelength bands and the inspector overlays observation vs reference plus annotations; uPlot renders thousands of points in <1ms, is ~40KB, and gives precise axis control. A tiny imperative React wrapper fits the one chart we need.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Chart.js/react-chartjs-2 (heavier, canvas abstraction overkill); Recharts (SVG, slow at hundreds of points, large); D3 from scratch (unnecessary engineering).

decisions.choice: Typed API client = backend OpenAPI 3.1 doc -> src/api/schema.d.ts via openapi-typescript 7.13, consumed by a hand-written typed fetch wrapper (client.ts) with per-resource modules; zod 4 validates the few payloads the globe renders directly (result meta, pixel spectrum, footprints).
decisions.rationale: Generating types from the backend's own OpenAPI makes the frontend/backend contract machine-checked and drift-proof; the thin fetch wrapper adds AbortController, error normalization and the mock switch. zod guards the specific network data that, if malformed, would crash the Cesium render path.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hand-maintained duplicate types (drift); a full generated SDK client like orval/openapi-fetch-everything (more magic than a GIS app needs); zod on every endpoint (runtime cost with little payoff for internal API).

decisions.choice: Result raster overlay supports BOTH an XYZ UrlTemplateImageryProvider (GeographicTilingScheme, equirectangular) and a SingleTileImageryProvider, selected by result metadata field tiling: 'xyz' | 'single'.
decisions.rationale: A single CRISM MTRDR footprint result is a small bbox where one PNG + rectangle (SingleTile) is simplest and avoids a tiling pipeline; larger or multi-observation results use XYZ tiles to bound memory. Letting backend metadata choose keeps the frontend generic.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: XYZ-only (forces a tiling step for a tiny demo result); SingleTile-only (does not scale, risks huge in-memory PNG decode).

decisions.choice: vite-plugin-static-copy 4.1.1 to copy Cesium's Assets/Workers/Widgets/ThirdParty into the build and set window.CESIUM_BASE_URL, NOT vite-plugin-cesium.
decisions.rationale: Verified vite-plugin-cesium was last published 2024-08 with a stale peer (vite >=2.7.1) and depends on serve-static/rollup-plugin-external-globals that are risky under Vite 7/8's Rollup. vite-plugin-static-copy explicitly supports vite ^6||^7||^8 and the manual CESIUM_BASE_URL approach is the officially documented, future-proof path.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: vite-plugin-cesium (unmaintained, Vite-major-lagging); bundling Cesium workers inline (large, brittle).

decisions.choice: Pixel location from clicks via camera.pickEllipsoid / globe.pick(ray) against the Mars ellipsoid, NOT scene.pickPosition; requestRenderMode enabled with explicit scene.requestRender() after every store-driven mutation.
decisions.rationale: With a flat EllipsoidTerrainProvider there is no depth buffer geometry for pickPosition to resolve, but pickEllipsoid returns an exact lon/lat on the Mars ellipsoid. requestRenderMode drastically cuts GPU/CPU use for a mostly-static globe; LayerManager and picking call requestRender() so changes still show.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: scene.pickPosition (unreliable/zero without terrain depth); continuous rendering (wasteful battery/CPU for a capstone demo).

decisions.choice: LayerManager is designed against a minimal injectable viewer interface (imageryLayers add/remove/raise/lower, dataSources, scene.requestRender) so its reconciliation logic is unit-testable without WebGL; Cesium-touching code is isolated under src/cesium/ and never imported by panels.
decisions.rationale: Cesium cannot run in jsdom (WebGL), so the only way to test the layer stack ordering/opacity/visibility logic is to decouple it from the real Viewer. This also enforces the architecture boundary that UI mutates the store, not Cesium.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Testing through the real Viewer (impossible headless); no tests on LayerManager (the most bug-prone reconciliation code goes unverified).

risks.risk: Trek / result tile Y-axis (tile-row) origin mismatch: Cesium's {y} may be flipped relative to the backend/Trek grid, producing upside-down or offset imagery.
risks.mitigation: Expose a reverseY flag per ImageryProviderSpec; verify on first render against a known feature (Nili Fossae) and switch {y}<->{reverseY}. Ground truth already verified Trek order {z}/{row=y}/{col=x} matches GeographicTilingScheme {z}/{y}/{x}; apply the same verification to backend result tiles before trusting them.

risks.risk: Longitude convention mismatch (east-positive vs west-positive, planetocentric vs planetographic, -180..180 vs 0..360) across footprints, basemap tiles, result tiles, gazetteer, and the pixel endpoint — would misplace footprints and mis-query pixels.
risks.mitigation: Pick ONE documented convention with backend (recommend east-positive planetocentric, -180..180), centralize conversion in utils/format.normalizeLon, and validate footprint centroids land on the right basemap features before shipping.

risks.risk: Cesium configured for Earth leaks through: wrong radii in picking/camera, Earth atmosphere/geocoder, or scene.pickPosition returning nothing without terrain depth (pixel inspector would fail).
risks.mitigation: Set Ellipsoid.default to Mars radii in main.tsx BEFORE any Viewer; disable Earth chrome via VIEWER_OPTIONS; use camera.pickEllipsoid/globe.pick for all lon/lat picks (never pickPosition) since terrain is a flat EllipsoidTerrainProvider.

risks.risk: Bleeding-edge toolchain (Vite 8 + plugin-react 6 Rolldown/oxc, TypeScript 7 native) could be unstable or break typescript-eslint, jeopardizing the 'must run' constraint for a capstone.
risks.mitigation: Pin the mature line: Vite 7.3.7 + @vitejs/plugin-react 5.2.0 + TypeScript 5.9.3 + Vitest 3.2.7 (all verified compatible; typescript-eslint 8.71 requires TS <6.1.0, which rules out TS7). Exact-version pins in package.json for reproducibility.

risks.risk: Offline/CI cannot reach trek.nasa.gov or the backend, so tests or demos appear broken.
risks.mitigation: VITE_USE_MOCKS=true serves all /api data from bundled tiny synthetic samples and a sample result PNG; vitest targets pure modules (geo/format/store/LayerManager via an injected fake viewer) and never hits the network or WebGL; the globe degrades gracefully to a dark base color when basemap tiles are unreachable.

risks.risk: A large SingleTile result PNG decoded in-memory could blow GPU/CPU memory and freeze the tab.
risks.mitigation: Default to tiling:'single' only for small CRISM-footprint bboxes; cap single-image dimensions and switch to XYZ tiles (bounded by GeographicTilingScheme + maximumLevel) for anything larger, selected by backend result metadata.

risks.risk: Trek basemap images may lack permissive CORS, so Cesium can load them for display but reading pixels (or stricter browsers) could fail.
risks.mitigation: Display-only use needs no CORS; if a browser/env blocks it, enable VITE_TREK_VIA_PROXY to route tiles through the Vite/nginx '/trek' proxy. Verified tiles return HTTP 200 image/jpeg so the display path works today.

risks.risk: Overstating science: a SAM spectral-angle hit could be read as a confirmed mineral deposit.
risks.mitigation: Enforced UI copy: SpectralAngleBadge, InspectorPanel, ResultsPanel and StatusBar all label results as 'candidate spectral match - not a confirmed mineral deposit'; show spectral angle + confidence rather than a binary 'detected' claim.

summary: Production-grade FastAPI backend for MarsGIS under `backend/`, serving the interactive map/dashboard. It is an async app (app factory + lifespan) with pydantic-settings config and CORS, a SQLModel data layer that defaults to zero-setup SQLite (footprints as GeoJSON text) and switches to PostgreSQL+PostGIS by env (footprints as SRID-104905 geometry), and a dialect-agnostic bbox-column strategy so spatial filtering works on both. Schema is managed by Alembic for Postgres and by metadata.create_all for SQLite dev (hybrid, chosen at startup by dialect). A job system runs out-of-the-box with NO extra infra: an in-process asyncio worker started in the app lifespan pulls from an asyncio.Queue, offloads the CPU-bound engine call to a bounded worker thread (anyio.to_thread), and writes status/progress to the analysis_jobs table; an optional arq+Redis worker (separate process, prod) is selected by config and writes to the same table. The science engine is consumed through a single `EngineAdapter` seam: in-process import of `marsgis_engine` for dev, and a subprocess/container path (ghcr.io/<account>/marsgis-engine) for isolation with CPU/memory/time rlimits. Raster results are served to CesiumJS on the fly from the output COG with rio-tiler (built on rasterio) over a CUSTOM Mars geographic TileMatrixSet that matches the verified NASA Trek equirectangular grid (z0 = 2 cols x 1 row), via `/api/results/{id}/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`, plus `/preview.png` + `/bounds` + `/legend.json` for a quick Cesium SingleTile overlay, and a GeoTIFF download. Startup seeding is idempotent and offline, loading a small catalogue of REAL Nili Fossae CRISM MTRDR observations (verified via PDS ODE), MICA reference minerals, and verified Trek map layers from bundled JSON. Public job submission is unauthenticated by default (demo), so it is strictly bounded (enum-only method = no arbitrary exec, body/AOI/count limits, per-client concurrency + hourly quota, per-job timeout and rlimits); an optional API-key gate is provided and flagged as mandatory for any real public deployment. Errors use an RFC 9457 problem+json envelope and all input is validated by pydantic. The backend consumes DTOs/enums from the data-model-and-contract concern and a narrow Python contract from the engine, and owns the persistence tables, all HTTP endpoints, the job runner, raster serving, and the Dockerfile.

decisions.choice: SQLModel (SQLAlchemy 2.x core) as ORM, single ASYNC engine for the whole app; aiosqlite for SQLite dev, asyncpg for Postgres
decisions.rationale: SQLModel unifies pydantic + SQLAlchemy so table models align with the contract DTOs with minimal duplication. A single async engine keeps request handlers and the in-process worker on one event loop; the worker offloads only the pure-compute engine call to a thread and keeps ALL DB writes on the loop, so no cross-thread session sharing is needed.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: A dual sync+async engine (sync session inside the worker thread) was rejected as unnecessary complexity once DB writes stay on the loop. Raw SQLAlchemy without SQLModel was rejected because it duplicates the pydantic DTO shapes.

decisions.choice: Dialect-agnostic spatial model: store footprint as GeoJSON TEXT in SQLite and Geometry(Polygon, 104905) in PostGIS, PLUS denormalised minx/miny/maxx/maxy columns on every spatial row
decisions.rationale: The bbox columns make map viewport/region filtering a plain numeric range query that works identically on both backends with no SpatiaLite dependency; PostGIS additionally gets ST_Intersects + a GiST index on the real geometry. GeoJSON text in SQLite is directly returnable to Cesium with no conversion.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Requiring SpatiaLite for SQLite was rejected (extra native dependency, breaks zero-setup). Storing only geometry and reprojecting/parsing for every list query was rejected as slow and dialect-coupled.

decisions.choice: Hybrid migrations: metadata.create_all on startup for SQLite dev; Alembic (`alembic upgrade head`) as source of truth for Postgres, run in CI/deploy and optionally on startup
decisions.rationale: Zero-setup dev must boot with no migration step; create_all is instant and sufficient for the single-process SQLite case. Postgres needs the PostGIS extension, the IAU 104905 spatial_ref_sys entry, geometry columns and GiST indexes that only a real migration expresses, so Alembic owns that path.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Alembic-only was rejected for adding friction to the primary dev path. create_all-only was rejected because it cannot create PostGIS extensions/indexes or evolve a live Postgres DB.

decisions.choice: In-process asyncio worker (asyncio.Queue + lifespan background task + bounded ThreadPool via anyio.to_thread) as the DEFAULT job backend, with an optional arq+Redis worker selected by JOB_BACKEND=arq
decisions.rationale: Meets the hard requirement that the product runs out-of-the-box with no extra infra. Both backends implement one `JobRunner` protocol and write identical status/progress to analysis_jobs, so the HTTP API and polling/SSE are backend-agnostic. arq+Redis gives horizontal scale and process isolation for prod without changing the API.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Celery was rejected as heavier and less async-native than arq. A naive BackgroundTasks-only approach was rejected because it has no queue, no concurrency cap, no cancellation, and no durable status.

decisions.choice: Engine invoked behind one `EngineAdapter` seam with two implementations: InProcessEngine (import marsgis_engine) for dev, Subprocess/ContainerEngine (python -m marsgis_engine run / ghcr.io image) for isolation
decisions.rationale: Keeps the exact engine signatures in one file so they can be pinned once the engine concern finalises them. In-process import is fastest for dev and CI; the subprocess/container path gives a hard process boundary where rlimits (RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_AS) and a wall-clock timeout bound untrusted public workloads.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hard-wiring in-process calls everywhere was rejected because it couples the API to the engine's import side effects and prevents isolation. Always-container was rejected as too slow and heavy for dev/CI.

decisions.choice: Serve result rasters with rio-tiler (on top of rasterio) over a CUSTOM morecantile Mars geographic TileMatrixSet (z0 = 2x1) matching the verified Trek equirectangular grid; immutable Cache-Control + optional on-disk tile cache
decisions.rationale: Cesium renders the Trek Mars basemap with a GeographicTilingScheme (2 columns x 1 row at level 0); result overlays MUST use the same scheme or they misregister. A WebMercator TMS (rio-tiler default, Earth) is wrong for Mars. Results are immutable, so tiles get `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and an optional disk cache.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Pre-tiling every result to disk (gdal2tiles) was rejected as slow and storage-heavy for on-demand analyses. Serving in WebMercator was rejected as geometrically wrong for a Mars globe.

decisions.choice: GeoJSON over the wire everywhere, coordinates in degrees (east longitude, planetocentric latitude), CRS treated as Mars 2000 geographic / IAU 104905 to match Trek
decisions.rationale: Cesium consumes GeoJSON and lon/lat degrees directly; Trek's own service advertises urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::104905, so aligning on it keeps footprints, basemaps and result overlays co-registered.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Projected (sinusoidal) coordinates over the API were rejected because the frontend would have to reproject. Earth EPSG:4326 was rejected as semantically wrong (Mars radii differ).

decisions.choice: Unauthenticated public job submission is allowed by default but hard-bounded; `REQUIRE_API_KEY` optional gate; method is a closed enum (no arbitrary exec)
decisions.rationale: The capstone demo should be usable without login, but an unauthenticated compute endpoint is a real abuse/DoS surface. Bounding it (enum method, body/AOI/class caps, per-client concurrency + hourly quota, per-job timeout + rlimits, catalogue-only observation ids, path-traversal-safe downloads) contains the blast radius; the API-key gate is there for any real deployment.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Fully open with no limits was rejected (DoS, cost). Mandatory auth by default was rejected as it breaks the zero-friction demo goal — but is explicitly flagged as required for public hosting.

decisions.choice: Bundle the seed JSON (CRISM catalogue, MICA minerals, map layers) inside backend/app/db/seeds/, shaped to the data-model contract; seeding is idempotent (upsert by id, guarded by SEED_ON_STARTUP)
decisions.rationale: Guarantees the app and CI boot fully offline with real, verified rows and no network dependency, satisfying the 'runs out of the box / tiny bundled data' constraint. Shaping to the contract keeps the frontend/API stable; upsert-by-id makes repeated startups safe.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Fetching the catalogue from PDS ODE at startup was rejected (violates offline boot, flaky). Owning the data shape independently of the contract concern was rejected to avoid schema drift.

contracts: HTTP REST API, all under `/api` (JSON unless noted). Health/meta: `GET /api/health`, `GET /api/version` (returns app + engine_version), OpenAPI at `/openapi.json`, docs at `/docs` (toggleable in prod).

Catalogue/reference endpoints: `GET /api/observations?region=&bbox=w,s,e,n&mineral=&limit=&offset=` and `GET /api/observations/{obs_id}` (ObservationRead incl. footprint GeoJSON + bbox); `GET /api/minerals?mineral_class=` and `GET /api/minerals/{id}` (MineralRead incl. wavelengths[] + reflectance[] arrays); `GET /api/layers` (MapLayerRead[] used by the frontend to configure Cesium imagery providers: url_template, product_id, tile_format jpg|png, tiling_scheme=geographic, z0=2x1, max_zoom, attribution, opacity, default_visible).

Job endpoints: `POST /api/jobs` -> 202 {job_id,status} (body JobCreate: observation_id, method=SAM [enum], mineral_classes[] [enum], threshold?, aoi? [bbox]); `GET /api/jobs?status=&mine=true` (per-client), `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}` (JobRead: status, progress 0-100, message, timestamps, result_id, error), `DELETE /api/jobs/{job_id}` (cancel), `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/events` (text/event-stream SSE live progress for the dashboard).

Result endpoints: `GET /api/results` and `GET /api/results/{id}` (ResultRead: method, mineral_classes, bounds [w,s,e,n], footprint GeoJSON, stats {per-class pixel counts, matched_area_km2, score min/max/mean, threshold}, classes [{class,label,color,count}], colormap, score_range, engine_version, provenance {observation_id, mineral ids, params}, disclaimer); `GET /api/results/{id}/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` (on-the-fly XYZ, Mars geographic TMS, immutable cache); `GET /api/results/{id}/preview.png` (downsampled full-extent PNG for Cesium SingleTileImageryProvider); `GET /api/results/{id}/bounds` ([w,s,e,n] degrees); `GET /api/results/{id}/legend.json` (colormap stops + class colors + labels + disclaimer); `GET /api/results/{id}/geotiff` (COG download, Content-Disposition).
Error envelope: RFC 9457 application/problem+json {type,title,status,detail,instance,errors?[]} for all 4xx/5xx incl. pydantic 422 validation; every response carries an `X-Request-ID`.

Persistence schema (owned here, shared with data-model-and-contract): tables observation, mineral, map_layer, analysis_job, result — field lists in app/db/models.py; this is the DB contract other concerns read.

Required-from-engine Python contract (consumed via app/services/engine_adapter.py): `marsgis_engine.__version__`; `fetch_observation(product_id, *, cache_dir, timeout) -> ObservationCube(cube_path, wavelengths, meta)`; `run_sam(cube, references, *, mineral_classes, threshold, aoi, out_dir, progress_cb) -> EngineResult(cog_path, preview_path, bounds, stats, classes, score_range, crs, width, height, engine_version)` — OR a single `analyze(EngineRequest, progress_cb) -> EngineResult`; CLI `python -m marsgis_engine run --request request.json --out <dir>` writing result.json+COG+preview for the subprocess/container path. Requirement on engine output: COG must be a valid cloud-optimized GeoTIFF carrying a readable Mars CRS so rio-tiler can reproject/tile it.

Build/deploy contract for infra: `backend/Dockerfile` (uvicorn, non-root, HEALTHCHECK on /api/health), env surface documented in backend/.env.example; a root `docker compose` (owned by infra concern) wires db/redis/backend/frontend — backend provides the service snippet in README.
dependencies_on_other_concerns: data-model-and-contract: consume the shared Pydantic v2 DTOs and enums (JobCreate, JobRead, ResultRead, ObservationRead, MineralRead, MapLayerRead; enums JobStatus{queued,running,succeeded,failed,cancelled}, AnalysisMethod{SAM,...}, MineralClass{carbonate,olivine,clay,sulfate,pyroxene,...}, LayerType{basemap,overlay}) and the problem+json error schema. Preferred delivery: a small pip-installable package (e.g. `marsgis-contracts` at repo-root `contracts/`) imported by backend; FALLBACK if not ready: backend defines local mirrors in app/schemas/ with a conformance test, switched to the shared import later. Also consume the canonical field spec/JSON Schema for the five entities and the seed-data shape (the actual small rows are bundled in backend/app/db/seeds/ but conform to this shape).

engine (hyperspectral science): consume the narrow Python API above via EngineAdapter (fetch_observation / run_sam|analyze returning EngineResult, plus __version__ and the `python -m marsgis_engine run` CLI + ghcr.io/<account>/marsgis-engine image). The engine owns CRISM MTRDR fetching via PDS service and SAM-vs-MICA computation; it must bundle a tiny sample/synthetic cube + MICA spectra so backend CI runs offline, and must emit a valid Mars-CRS COG + preview + bounds + stats. Backend installs it editable (`pip install -e ../engine`) for the in-process path.

frontend (React+Vite+Cesium): a CONSUMER of this API, not consumed here. Backend must expose CORS for the frontend origin(s) and keep the layers/results/tiles contract above stable; the GeographicTilingScheme (z0 2x1) and GeoJSON degree conventions are the shared assumption.

infra/deploy: provides the root docker compose, Postgres+PostGIS and (prod) Redis services, and GHCR publishing of the engine image. Backend consumes DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL / ENGINE_* from that environment and provides the Dockerfile + env contract.

summary:
The science-engine is a standalone, reproducible Python package (`marsgis_engine`) living entirely under `engine/`. It is importable by the backend AND exposed as a CLI (`marsgis-engine`) that is the entrypoint of the standalone image `ghcr.io/<account>/marsgis-engine`. Its single responsibility: turn an analysis-ready CRISM MTRDR cube (ENVI .img/.hdr, already calibrated + map-projected) plus a MICA reference spectrum into (a) a float32 spectral-angle raster and (b) a thresholded "candidate-match" mask, both written as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs that preserve the input's Mars CRS/affine, accompanied by a machine-readable provenance JSON and a human-readable report.

Pipeline (science/pipeline.py): load cube (SPy for spectra+wavelengths+bad-band-list, rasterio/GDAL for CRS+affine) -> normalize wavelengths to nm -> build a good-band mask from the ENVI `bbl` + a diagnostic wavelength window (default IR 1.0-2.6 um where Nili Fossae carbonate ~2.3/2.5 um, olivine broad ~1 um, Fe/Mg-smectite 1.9/2.3 um features live) -> load MICA .tab reference and resample it onto the cube's wavelength grid -> optional convex-hull continuum removal on both -> vectorized numpy Spectral Angle Mapper per pixel (chunked by row-block to bound memory) -> write angle COG (radians, NaN nodata) + candidate COG (uint8 0/1, 255 nodata) -> emit provenance.json + report.txt. The engine performs NO re-calibration and NO reprojection: MTRDR is analysis-ready I/F, so outputs inherit the input grid losslessly; tiling/reprojection is the backend/frontend concern.

Scientific honesty is a first-class design goal: the continuous angle raster is always retained (not just the binary mask), outputs are labeled "candidate" everywhere, the known caveat that MICA type spectra are ratioed I/F while scene pixels are un-ratioed I/F is documented and partially mitigated by SAM's albedo-invariance + optional continuum removal + wavelength windowing, and both the report and provenance carry an explicit "candidate != confirmed deposit" disclaimer. Tests run fully offline on a tiny synthetic ENVI cube + synthetic reference, with a few KB of bundled public-domain MICA .tab files for integration.

decisions.choice: Package as src/ layout, PEP 621 pyproject.toml, console_scripts entry `marsgis-engine = marsgis_engine.cli:main`; ship `py.typed`.
decisions.rationale: src/ prevents accidental import of the un-built package and forces testing the installed artifact; a single declarative pyproject drives both pip install (for backend import) and the Docker build; typed marker lets the backend get type info.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Flat layout + setup.py (import-path ambiguity, legacy); a Poetry-only build (poetry/pnpm/yarn absent on host, npm/pip only).

decisions.choice: Dual reader: spectral (SPy) `envi.open` for the data cube, wavelengths, bad-band list (bbl), and data-ignore-value; rasterio/GDAL for the geotransform + CRS. Normalize all wavelengths to nanometers internally.
decisions.rationale: SPy parses ENVI spectral metadata (wavelength/bbl/units) that GDAL exposes weakly, while GDAL/rasterio parses the ENVI `map info`/coordinate-system-string into a proper affine+CRS. CRISM .hdr uses nm, MICA .tab uses um, so a single internal unit (nm) removes a whole class of bugs.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Pure rasterio (drops wavelength + bbl, fatal for SAM); pure SPy (weak/absent georeferencing).

decisions.choice: Vectorized numpy SAM over reshaped (npixels, nbands) arrays, processed in row-block chunks via windowed reads/writes; angle in radians.
decisions.rationale: Explicit implementation gives full control over NaN/bad-band masking, scale-invariance, and clipping arccos args to [-1,1]; chunking bounds memory for ~450-band ~500x500 cubes (hundreds of MB) in float32.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: spectral.algorithms.spectral_angles (opaque masking/NaN handling); naive per-pixel Python loop (orders of magnitude too slow).

decisions.choice: Emit BOTH a float32 angle raster (radians, lower=better, NaN nodata) and a uint8 candidate mask (0/1 with 255=nodata); never only the binary mask.
decisions.rationale: Preserving the continuous angle keeps the uncertainty visible and lets the frontend/analyst re-threshold without recompute; honest about match confidence.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Mask-only output (destroys uncertainty, invites overclaiming).

decisions.choice: Write COGs by first writing a tiled interim GTiff with windowed writes, then `rasterio.shutil.copy(..., driver="COG")` to produce a validated Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF.
decisions.rationale: GDAL's COG driver is effectively CreateCopy/single-pass (confirmed `w+v`, not update), which conflicts with chunked windowed writing; the GTiff->COG copy reconciles chunked compute with a true, overview-bearing COG.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Direct windowed writes into driver=COG (unsupported write pattern); plain GTiff (not cloud-optimized for the map tile server).

decisions.choice: Reference resampling: default 1-D linear interpolation over the wavelength overlap (out-of-range bands masked), optional FWHM-aware Gaussian via `spectral.BandResampler` when FWHM is present.
decisions.rationale: Linear interp is robust and dependency-light; Gaussian band-response resampling is more physically correct when the reference is higher-resolution and FWHM is known.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Nearest-neighbor (aliases narrow absorption features); requiring both grids identical (brittle).

decisions.choice: Convex-hull continuum removal is optional and OFF by default; when enabled it is applied (chunked) to both pixel and reference spectra within the diagnostic window.
decisions.rationale: SAM is already invariant to multiplicative albedo scaling, so continuum removal is an enhancement (emphasizes band shape, mitigates the ratioed-MICA vs un-ratioed-scene mismatch), not a requirement; per-pixel hull is O(npix*nbands) so it is opt-in and window-restricted.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Always-on continuum removal (cost + not always desired); band-depth-only parameters (less general than SAM shape matching).

decisions.choice: Engine does NOT fetch the MTRDR cube or re-calibrate it; it receives a local .img/.hdr path. It bundles a few KB of public-domain MICA .tab references (carbonate, olivine, fe_smectite) + synthetic test fixtures, and offers an opt-in `fetch-references` command for the rest.
decisions.rationale: Honors the hard constraint (no bulk downloads; runs offline in CI); MTRDR acquisition is the backend/data concern; MICA type spectra are tiny PDS public-domain ASCII, legitimately bundled as the 'tiny sample data'.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Bundling full MTRDR cubes (bulk data, violates constraint); fetching MICA at runtime unconditionally (breaks offline CI).

decisions.choice: CRS fallback: read CRS/affine from the ENVI header; if GDAL cannot resolve the Mars datum, attach a configurable default Mars 2000 equirectangular WKT and LOG it as ASSUMED; never silently drop georeferencing.
decisions.rationale: ENVI+Mars datums frequently fail to map to a known authority code in GDAL; the output must stay georeferenced and the assumption must be auditable.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Writing a CRS-less raster (unusable as a map layer); hardcoding a single Mars CRS with no override.

decisions.choice: Reproducibility: provenance JSON records sha256 of every input, pinned library + GDAL versions, host platform, and a timestamp that defaults to UTC-now but accepts `--timestamp` (including a fixed placeholder) for deterministic builds/tests.
decisions.rationale: MSc capstone + production grade demands auditability and byte-reproducible test outputs; the placeholder satisfies the task's 'timestamp placeholder' requirement without sacrificing real runs.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Always embedding wall-clock time (non-reproducible outputs break golden-file tests).

decisions.choice: CLI matches the required shape `marsgis-engine run --cube ... --mineral carbonate --method SAM --threshold ... --out ...`, plus `info`, `list-minerals`, `fetch-references`, and `version` subcommands; `--mineral` is an alias resolved via data/minerals.json (carbonate->mg_carbonate, olivine->mg_olivine, clay->fe_smectite), overridable by `--reference PATH`.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the exact contract the orchestrator specified while giving operators inspection (`info`) and discoverability (`list-minerals`); alias layer hides MICA naming without hiding it from power users.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Only a single `run` command (poor DX, no way to inspect a cube's bands/CRS before a long run).

continuum_removed(spectra, wavelengths)->ndarray: for each spectrum computes the upper convex hull (monotone-chain over (wavelength,value)), linearly interpolates the hull across all bands, returns spectrum/hull in (0,1] (absorption depth = 1-value). Vectorized across pixels where possible, otherwise loops within a numpy row-chunk (documented O(npix*nbands); recommended on a narrow window). remove_reference_continuum(ref_vals, wl) convenience. NaN-safe (hull computed on finite bands only). Pure numpy/scipy, no numba dependency (optional accel noted in docstring).

sam_angles(pixels, reference, *, valid_band_mask)->angles: pixels shape (npix,nbands); computes per-pixel angle = arccos( clip( dot(t,r)/(||t||*||r||), -1, 1 ) ) over valid bands, with per-pixel finite-band handling (bands that are NaN in a given pixel excluded pairwise), returning NaN where a pixel has < MIN_OVERLAP_BANDS finite bands or zero norm. threshold_mask(angles, threshold_rad)->uint8 (1 where angle<=threshold & finite, 0 where >threshold, 255 where NaN). Documented invariants: identical spectrum->0, scaled spectrum->0 (albedo invariance), orthogonal->pi/2. Operates block-wise; no full-cube materialization required.

CRISM MTRDR = Map-Projected Targeted Reduced Data Records, a PDS4 derived product bundle 'mrocr_4001' at pds-geosciences.wustl.edu, organized under mtrdr/<year>/ with a collection inventory CSV + XML; products are ENVI rasters (.img data + .hdr header) with PDS .xml labels, map-projected and atmospherically/photometrically corrected (analysis-ready; the TER source is standardized for illumination/geometry and atmospheric gas removal) — i.e. must NOT be re-calibrated by the engine.

summary: Verified, reachable fetch strategy for every MarsGIS data source this run (2026-10-11, macOS host). All five requested sources were reached live with tools. (1) PDS Orbital Data Explorer (ODE) REST API is the CRISM MTRDR discovery layer: base https://oderest.rsl.wustl.edu/live2/, a spatial query over the Nili Fossae bbox [74,20,78,24] returns 23 MTRDR products with WKT footprints + full metadata (results=m) and authoritative file-URL lists (results=f). (2) The MTRDR archive is static HTTPS on the PDS Geosciences node; one observation = ENVI cubes (_if/_in/_sr/_su) + DDR geometry (_de) + wavelength table (_wv) + browse RGBs; the primary _if cube is ENVI BSQ float32, 843x828x489 bands, nm wavelengths, ignore=65535, and GDAL/rasterio read it directly (verified with gdalinfo). (3) The CRISM MICA reference library is static ASCII .tab + PDS .lbl; carbonate = crism_typespec_fe_ca_carbonate.tab (480 rows, col1 wavelength µm, col2 ratioed I/F corrected = the SAM reference), olivine = crism_typespec_fe_olivine.tab, clays = al/fe_smectite. (4) USGS SIM 3292 is available as a LIVE OGC API-Features vector service (pygeoapi) returning GeoJSON with bbox filtering (units/contacts/structure), plus static downloads — so the geologic map overlays as queryable vectors, not a flat raster. (5) Correct Mars Trek EQ product ids were confirmed via the Trek search index + per-product WMTSCapabilities: Viking (jpg) and MOLA ClrShade (jpg) basemaps, MOLA global DEM mola128_mola64_merge_90Nto90S_SimpleC_clon0 (png), and THEMIS Day IR THEMIS_DayIR_ControlledMosaics_100m_v2_oct2018 (png); the earlier guessed MOLA-DEM/THEMIS ids 404'd and are wrong. Default fetch posture is live-proxy-with-cache (no bulk mirroring, per the hard constraint); CI/offline runs on a bundled, GDAL-readable synthetic ENVI cube + synthetic carbonate reference that I generated and validated end-to-end (SAM separates carbonate from olivine, 0.23° vs 7.65°). Deliverables map cleanly onto the already-present shared Pydantic contracts in backend/app/schemas (LayerSource, ObservationSummary, DatasetAccess).

decisions.alternatives_rejected: PDS4 registry / pds.nasa.gov search API (heavier, less footprint-centric); scraping Apache directory listings (brittle, no spatial filter); bulk archive mirror (violates the no-bulk-download constraint).

summary:
DevOps & reproducibility design for MarsGIS: a monorepo (frontend/, backend/, engine/, docker/, docs/, .github/) wired together by Docker + `docker compose`, a Makefile, and GitHub Actions, with Docker as the single source of truth for the runtime environment.

Core choices, grounded in facts verified this session:
- Python is pinned to 3.12 everywhere (containers + CI), NOT the host's 3.14. 3.12 has the broadest wheel coverage across the full scientific/geo stack (numpy 2, scikit-learn, pyproj, shapely, fiona, rasterio, FastAPI/pydantic). The host's 3.14 is used only for best-effort local tooling; `make`/compose/CI all run 3.12.
- The engine base image is `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` (multi-stage), installing rasterio from PyPI wheels (which bundle their own GDAL >=3.8) and the pure-python `spectral` package, so there is NO system/wheel GDAL version-skew, no compiler, no libgdal-dev, and the image stays small with no bundled archive. The documented alternative is `ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-<pin>` for when the full GDAL/OGR CLI suite is required.
- All three images (engine, backend, frontend) are multi-stage, run as a non-root user (uid 10001), and are published to GHCR as `ghcr.io/${GHCR_OWNER}/marsgis-{engine,backend,frontend}`. The engine is the headline standalone artifact `ghcr.io/${GHCR_OWNER}/marsgis-engine` with a `marsgis-engine` CLI entrypoint.
- compose runs db (postgis) + backend + frontend, with redis+worker, the engine, and titiler behind opt-in `profiles`. Healthchecks and localhost-only port binds throughout. The backend also supports a zero-setup SQLite path (DATABASE_URL swap) so a developer can run it without the db container.
- Reproducible installs via fully pinned, hash-locked requirements.txt (`pip --require-hashes`); versions derive from git tags (SemVer) via setuptools-scm/hatch-vcs; releases build & push multi-arch images with SBOM + provenance attestations; Zenodo archives each tagged release (via the GitHub integration + .zenodo.json + CITATION.cff) and run outputs are archived with their input provenance and the engine image digest.

Repo-layout rule to avoid collisions with other concerns: this concern owns root infra files, docker/, .github/, and the per-service Dockerfile/.dockerignore/entrypoint/nginx-config files that MUST live inside frontend/, backend/, engine/ (the task's explicitly-expected shared contract files). It does NOT own any application source under those dirs.

decisions.choice: Engine (and backend) base image = python:3.12-slim-bookworm, multi-stage, with rasterio installed from PyPI manylinux wheels (vendored GDAL >=3.8) and the pure-python `spectral` package.
decisions.rationale: Verified this session: rasterio 1.5.2 ships official binary wheels whose vendored GDAL (>=3.8) requires no system libgdal, no compiler, and no libgdal-dev; spectral 0.25 is pure-python (py3-none-any, numpy-only). This decouples the Python version from any GDAL-base-image Ubuntu coupling, pins Python exactly to 3.12, eliminates system-vs-wheel GDAL version skew, keeps the image small, and needs no bundled archive. rasterio/pyproj/rasterio.warp cover reprojection and rio-cogeo covers COG/tiling, so the gdalinfo CLI is not required for the SAM pipeline.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-<pin> — kept as a DOCUMENTED fallback for when the full GDAL/OGR CLI suite or exotic drivers/PROJ grids are needed. Rejected as default because (a) its Python version is tied to the Ubuntu base: verified ubuntu-small-latest/GDAL-3.13 is Ubuntu 26.04 + Python 3.14, so a 3.12 pin forces an older GDAL-3.9..3.12 tag (Ubuntu 24.04), coupling GDAL and Python choices; (b) adding pip-installed rasterio on top risks GDAL double-install or a source build against system GDAL. If adopted, pin ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-3.12.x by digest.

decisions.choice: Pin Python to 3.12 in all containers and CI; the host's Python 3.14 is NOT the authoritative environment.
decisions.rationale: Reproducibility means one pinned interpreter for the whole dependency tree, not 'whatever the host has'. 3.12 has been stable longest and every scientific/geo dependency (numpy 2, scikit-learn, pyproj, shapely, fiona, GeoAlchemy2, FastAPI/pydantic) ships 3.12 wheels; 3.14 (Oct 2025) is new and some transitive deps may still lack wheels, risking slow source builds. Docker/compose/CI are the source of truth. For developers who want a non-Docker local venv, docs recommend installing a 3.12 interpreter alongside the host 3.14 (uv or pyenv) as best-effort; CI uses actions/setup-python@v5 with python-version 3.12.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Pinning to 3.14 to match the host: rejected even though rasterio and spectral both support 3.14 (verified) — chasing the newest for two libs does not justify risking the rest of the tree, and the host interpreter must not define the artifact.

decisions.choice: Pin the frontend build to node:24-bookworm-slim (Active LTS) with .nvmrc=24; host node 26 is for local dev only.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the Python reasoning: pin an established LTS with universal ecosystem/tooling support for reproducible builds rather than the brand-new line the host happens to run (26). Docker/CI node 24 is authoritative; local dev on host 26 is fine.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: node:26 (match host): newest LTS line, broader risk of tooling lag; node:22 maintenance LTS: older than needed.

decisions.choice: Per-service build contexts (./frontend, ./backend, ./engine); Dockerfiles and their build-time config co-located with each service; top-level docker/ holds only RUNTIME-mounted assets.
decisions.rationale: Keeps each build context tight (fast builds, small layers, no cross-service leakage). docker/ meaningfully holds the postgres PostGIS-bootstrap init SQL (mounted into the db container) and optional titiler config, which are not baked into any image. Backend entrypoint and frontend nginx config live beside their source because they are COPYed into those images at build time.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Single repo-root build context with one .dockerignore: bloats every image's context with sibling concerns' trees; central docker/ dir holding all Dockerfiles: breaks tight contexts and splits each image from its source.

decisions.choice: docker compose (v2 plugin, invoked as `docker compose`); optional services (engine, worker/redis, titiler) gated behind compose profiles; all ports bound to 127.0.0.1 in dev.
decisions.rationale: Host provides the compose plugin (no standalone docker-compose). Profiles keep the default `make up` lean (db+backend+frontend) while allowing `--profile worker|tiles|engine` opt-in. Localhost binds avoid exposing unauthenticated dev services to the LAN.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: standalone docker-compose binary (absent on host); always-on redis/titiler (unnecessary weight for the common path).

decisions.choice: Database image postgis/postgis:17-3.5 (matches host psql 17); arm64 handled via emulation or an arm64-capable alternative.
decisions.rationale: Verified this session: postgis/postgis:17-3.5 exists and `latest` currently resolves to it; aligns with the host's Postgres 17. The SQLite fallback (DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///...) covers zero-setup dev without this container.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: postgres:17 + manual PostGIS install (fragile); pinning `latest` (non-reproducible).

decisions.choice: All images multi-stage, non-root (uid/gid 10001), venv-copy pattern, OCI provenance labels, no bundled data archive.
decisions.rationale: Smallest attack surface and image size; non-root satisfies production/CI hardening; venv-copy keeps the runtime stage free of build tools. The 'no bundled archive' hard constraint is enforced by .dockerignore excluding data/ plus a pre-commit large-file guard. Only tiny synthetic samples (authored by us) ride along for offline CI.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: single-stage root images (larger, unsafe); baking sample archives into images (violates the no-bulk-data constraint).

decisions.choice: Version derives from git tags (SemVer) via setuptools-scm / hatch-vcs; Conventional Commits + Keep-a-Changelog; releases triggered by pushing a vX.Y.Z tag.
decisions.rationale: Single source of truth for version is the git tag — no VERSION file to drift across frontend/backend/engine. docker/metadata-action turns the tag into image tags (X.Y.Z, X.Y, latest, sha). Conventional Commits enables automated changelog/release notes (release-please or git-cliff optional).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hand-maintained VERSION file (drifts in a monorepo); per-package independent versioning (overkill for one coordinated capstone).

decisions.choice: Reproducible dependency installs via fully pinned, hash-locked requirements.txt consumed with `pip install --require-hashes`; pyproject.toml carries metadata + the console_script entrypoint; Dependabot keeps pins fresh.
decisions.rationale: Hash-locked installs make container builds bit-reproducible and defend against tampered/typosquatted packages. pyproject provides the marsgis-engine entrypoint and dev extras. Dependabot (pip/npm/docker/actions) proposes grouped bumps so pinning is not a maintenance dead-end.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Unpinned ranges (non-reproducible, supply-chain risk); poetry/uv-only lockfiles (uv not installed on host; pip is guaranteed present).

decisions.choice: CI split into frontend, python (backend+engine), and docker-build jobs; a separate release workflow builds & pushes multi-arch images to GHCR with SBOM + provenance attestations on tag.
decisions.rationale: Fast parallel feedback; the python job runs ruff + pytest fully offline using the bundled synthetic sample; docker-build validates all three images build and smoke-tests `marsgis-engine --help` without pushing on PRs. Release pushes linux/amd64+arm64 and attaches SBOM/provenance for a verifiable, citable artifact.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: One monolithic job (slow, unclear failures); pushing images on every PR (pollutes GHCR, needs write creds on untrusted PRs).

decisions.choice: Licensing: MIT for code, CC0 for the tiny synthetic sample data, CC-BY-4.0 for docs; NASA source data is fetched via services and NOT redistributed in the repo.
decisions.rationale: MIT is the conventional permissive choice for an open MSc capstone and maximizes reuse. The 'fetch via API, no bulk downloads' constraint means we never vendor NASA archives; docs/DATA_LICENSES.md records attributions (NASA/JPL-Caltech/JHUAPL, NASA/GSFC, USGS/NASA, NASA Mars Trek) and the mandatory disclaimer that a candidate spectral match is never a confirmed mineral deposit.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Apache-2.0 (fine, but MIT is simpler and the task recommends it); redistributing NASA data (violates the no-bulk-download constraint).

decisions.choice: Zenodo archiving via the GitHub-Zenodo integration + .zenodo.json + CITATION.cff; run OUTPUTS archived separately with input provenance and the engine image digest.
decisions.rationale: Each tagged GitHub Release gets a DOI automatically; .zenodo.json/CITATION.cff supply authored metadata and a citable record for the capstone. Archiving a classification run alongside the exact engine image digest and input observation id makes results reproducible and citable.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Manual Zenodo uploads (error-prone, no provenance link).

decisions.choice: Pre-commit enforces secret and large-file hygiene (gitleaks, detect-private-key, check-added-large-files max-kb=256) plus ruff/prettier/hadolint; CI re-runs the same checks.
decisions.rationale: The large-file guard operationalizes the 'no bulk archives' constraint at commit time; gitleaks/detect-private-key stop credential leaks since .env files and data live in the repo tree. Running the same hooks in CI prevents bypass.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: CI-only checks (slower feedback, easier to merge mistakes); no size guard (archives slip in).

decisions.choice: Security posture of the dev stack is explicit: compose binds all services to 127.0.0.1 and ships NO authentication; production requires auth + TLS behind a gateway.
decisions.rationale: The backend API and titiler are unauthenticated in the dev compose. Localhost-only binds make that acceptable for local dev, but this must be flagged: deploying this compose as-is would expose an unauthenticated API. README and docs state that production needs authentication, TLS termination, and a reverse proxy/gateway in front of the backend.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Silently exposing 0.0.0.0 ports (unauthenticated service on the network); adding half-baked auth to the dev stack (owned by the backend concern, out of scope here).

summary:
The shared MarsGIS contract that frontend (TS), backend (Pydantic) and engine all build against. One source of truth: backend/app/schemas (Pydantic v2) is authoritative; contracts/openapi.yaml is GENERATED from it (so it cannot silently drift); frontend/src/types mirrors it and is tsc --strict clean; contracts/enums.json pins every closed vocabulary + cross-cutting default for all three languages. contract_version = 1.0.0.

COORDINATES: all bbox/footprint/bounds are Mars IAU 2000 degrees (lon east-positive [-180,180], planetocentric lat [-90,90]) — NOT Earth WGS84. Frontend must configure a Mars ellipsoid.

DATA MODEL (entities -> key fields; relationships in parentheses):
- Observation (id=native obs id e.g. "frt00003e12"; instrument; product_type; title; provider; region; bbox[w,s,e,n]; center{lon,lat}; footprint GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon; acquired_at; resolution_m; analysis_suitable:bool; thumbnail_url; target="Mars"; dataset_id?->Dataset; spectral:SpectralSummary{band_count,wavelength_min/max_nm,sampling_nm,ranges[]}; quality:QualityFlags{spike/atmospheric/photometric_corrected, score 0..1, notes}; source_url; browse_url; created/updated_at). ObservationSummary is the list projection (keeps footprint+bbox for the map; drops spectral detail/quality/source_url).
- Dataset (id; title; provider; kind:DatasetKind; instrument?; product_type?; spatial_extent?; temporal_extent?; license; attribution; access:DatasetAccess{service,url,auth_required}; observation_count) — groups/sources observations.
- SpectralReference / ...Summary ("minerals"): (id slug; mineral label; mineral_class; source e.g. "CRISM MICA"; spectrum_type reflectance|continuum_removed; resampled_to e.g. "CRISM_MTRDR"; point_count; wavelength_min/max_nm; diagnostic_features_nm[]; color hex). Full record adds wavelength[]+reflectance[] (equal length, validated).
- AnalysisJob (id; observation_id->Observation; algorithm:AnalysisAlgorithm; reference_id->SpectralReference; params:SamParams{threshold_rad=0.10, continuum_removed=true, wavelength_subset_nm=[1000,2600], bands?, output_resolution_m?}; status:JobStatus; progress 0..1; message; result_id?->AnalysisResult; error?:JobError{code,message,retriable}; created/updated/started/finished_at). AnalysisJobCreate = {observation_id, algorithm, reference_id, params?}.
- AnalysisResult (id; job_id->; observation_id; algorithm; reference_id; mineral snapshot; rasters:ResultRasters{cog,angle,mask,score? each RasterAsset{href,role:AssetRole,media_type,units,value_range,nodata,w,h,size}}; bounds[w,s,e,n]; value_range[min,max]; legend:Legend; summary_stats:SummaryStats{pixel_count,valid,detected,detected_fraction,min/max/mean/median/std,threshold_rad,reference_id,mineral,histogram?,caveat}; map_layer:MapLayer (ready-to-add Cesium layer, type=result_tiles); provenance_id->Provenance; caveat).
- MapLayer (id; type:LayerType; title; is_base; default_visible; source:LayerSource{url_template, tiling_scheme, tile_order:zyx|zxy, tile_size, file_extension jpg|png, level_zero_tiles_x/y, min/max_zoom, tile_matrix_set?, provider}; style:LayerStyle{opacity,colormap?,value_range?,z_index}; attribution; availability:LayerAvailability{status verified|unconfirmed|unavailable, checked_at, sample_tile_url, http_status}; bounds?; legend?).
- Provenance (id; result_id->; job_id; observation_id; reference_id; engine_image=ghcr.io/<account>/marsgis-engine:<tag>; engine_version; software:SoftwareComponent[]{name,version}; source_ids[]; source_urls[]; steps:ProvenanceStep[]{order,name,software,version,params,started/finished_at,status,message}; params; inputs/outputs_checksums; started/finished_at; timestamp; caveat).

REST API (base /api; full request/response in contracts/openapi.yaml, 12 paths / 51 component schemas, validated OpenAPI 3.1). JSON list envelope Paginated<T>={items,total,limit,offset,next_offset}; small lists ListResponse<T>={items}. Uniform error body ErrorResponse={code,message,detail?,request_id?,errors[]} (also for 422).
- GET /api/health -> HealthResponse{status, version, contract_version, git_sha, time, components{db,engine,tiler,queue:{status,detail,latency_ms}}, implemented_algorithms}.
- GET /api/layers?type&is_base&availability -> ListResponse<MapLayer>.
- GET /api/observations?instrument&product_type&region&bbox="w,s,e,n"&suitable&q&limit(50,max200)&offset&sort -> Paginated<ObservationSummary>.
- GET /api/observations/{id} -> Observation (404 if absent).
- GET /api/minerals?class&source&q -> ListResponse<SpectralReferenceSummary> (no arrays).
- GET /api/minerals/{id} -> SpectralReference (adds wavelength[]/reflectance[]; ADDED beyond task list so the spectral plot has data).
- POST /api/analysis-jobs (body AnalysisJobCreate, optional Idempotency-Key header) -> 202 AnalysisJob (status=queued) + Location header. Validates: observation exists & analysis_suitable, reference exists, algorithm implemented (else 422).
- GET /api/analysis-jobs?status&observation_id&limit&offset -> Paginated<AnalysisJob> (ADDED list endpoint). GET /api/analysis-jobs/{id} -> AnalysisJob (poll).
- GET /api/results/{id} -> AnalysisResult.
- GET /api/results/{id}/download?asset=primary_metric|sam_angle|detection_mask|match_score -> binary Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF.
- GET /api/results/{id}/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?colormap&rescale -> PNG tile (geographic scheme), 204 for empty tiles.
- GET /api/provenance/{id} -> Provenance (id from AnalysisResult.provenance_id).

JOB LIFECYCLE: POST creates queued. Worker: queued->running (set started_at, stream progress/message via provenance steps). Terminal: running->succeeded (set result_id, progress=1, finished_at) or running->failed (set error, finished_at); a pre-start validation failure may go queued->failed. Terminal states have no outgoing transitions (JOB_STATUS_TRANSITIONS in enums.json). Clients poll GET /api/analysis-jobs/{id}; v1 has no websockets. Cancellation is deliberately out of scope for v1 (task's 4-state enum kept).

RESULT->MAP CONTRACT (how a result becomes a Cesium layer): the engine writes a COG of the SAM angle in geographic CRS (IAU Mars 2000, lon/lat deg). The backend returns AnalysisResult.map_layer (type=result_tiles) whose source.url_template = /api/results/{id}/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png, tiling_scheme=geographic, tile_order=zxy, level_zero_tiles_x=2/y=1, tile_size=256, min/max_zoom; map_layer.bounds = result.bounds; map_layer.style.value_range + colormap; map_layer.legend = result.legend (with units + the candidate-not-confirmed caveat). Frontend builds a Cesium UrlTemplateImageryProvider with GeographicTilingScheme({numberOfLevelZeroTilesX:2,Y:1}) and Rectangle.fromDegrees(...bounds). Geographic (NOT Web Mercator) tiling is mandatory so result tiles register exactly with the NASA Trek basemaps (same equirectangular 2x1 grid). The tile endpoint renders PNG from the COG via rio-tiler/titiler using colormap+value_range with transparent nodata — color is baked server-side so the client needs no raster math.

SAFETY: every AnalysisResult, its SummaryStats, its Legend, and its Provenance carry a required `caveat` string = CANDIDATE_MATCH_CAVEAT ("Candidate spectral match ... NOT a confirmed mineral deposit ..."). The contract makes it structurally impossible to return a detection without the caveat.

decisions.choice: Single source of truth = Pydantic v2; contracts/openapi.yaml is generated from it; TS is a hand-written mirror that is tsc --strict verified.
decisions.rationale: Backend is FastAPI/Python (GDAL/rasterio/spectral ecosystem), so Pydantic already governs the wire at runtime. Generating OpenAPI from the models means the committed spec can never drift from the server; TS mirrors the same shapes and is compile-checked.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Hand-authored OpenAPI as source (drifts from code); codegen TS from OpenAPI (adds a build-time toolchain dependency and awkward generated names — kept a clean hand-written mirror instead, with CI equality check as the guard).

decisions.choice: Result tiles use a GEOGRAPHIC (equirectangular, 2x1 @ z0) tiling scheme, not Web Mercator.
decisions.rationale: The verified NASA Trek Mars basemaps are equirectangular 2x1@z0 and Cesium's Mars globe uses GeographicTilingScheme; serving result overlays in the same scheme makes them register pixel-for-pixel with the basemap with no reprojection.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Web Mercator XYZ (industry default on Earth) — wrong for a planetary globe; would misalign with Trek and distort high latitudes.

decisions.choice: Deliver the Result->Map display object as a ready MapLayer embedded in AnalysisResult (plus explicit bounds/value_range/legend fields).
decisions.rationale: The frontend layer manager treats catalog layers and result layers uniformly; one object carries tiles url template + scheme + bounds + legend + value range, so adding a result to the map is a single append.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Returning only raster paths and making the client assemble the tiling scheme/legend (duplicated logic, drift risk between client and tiler).

decisions.choice: Async job model: POST returns 202 + queued job, client polls GET /api/analysis-jobs/{id}.
decisions.rationale: SAM over a CRISM cube is seconds-to-minutes; a queue (Redis worker, implied by repo .gitignore) decouples the request. Polling is trivial for the frontend and CI.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Synchronous POST (ties up a request worker, times out); websockets/SSE (unnecessary complexity for v1 — progress field + poll suffices).

decisions.choice: extra=forbid on every wire model; a contract_version string gated by enums.json.
decisions.rationale: Strict models catch typos and accidental fields on both sides immediately; an explicit version lets all three concerns detect an incompatible contract.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Lenient models that ignore unknown fields (hide mismatches until runtime).

decisions.choice: algorithm enum includes SAM|SID|BAND_RATIO but only SAM is implemented in v1 (IMPLEMENTED_ALGORITHMS_V1); others -> HTTP 422.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the type stable for the roadmap without promising endpoints that return nothing; the first experiment (carbonate SAM vs MICA) is fully supported.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: SAM-only enum (churns the type when SID lands); accepting all and failing in the engine (fails late, worse UX).

decisions.choice: Observation.id is the provider-native observation id (opaque string, e.g. lowercase 'frt00003e12'), not a surrogate UUID.
decisions.rationale: CRISM obs ids are globally unique, human-meaningful on the map, and match what the PDS ODE API returns (verified by the data-access concern's seed).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Surrogate UUID + unique(provider,external_id) — extra indirection with no benefit for read-mostly reference data.

decisions.choice: Split minerals into Summary (list, no arrays) and full SpectralReference (/api/minerals/{id}, with wavelength[]/reflectance[]); added /api/minerals/{id} and GET /api/analysis-jobs list beyond the task's endpoint list.
decisions.rationale: The list stays light for the picker; the spectral plot needs the arrays; a jobs list is needed for a dashboard. Additions are non-conflicting and documented.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Returning full arrays in the list (heavy, unused by the picker).

decisions.choice: LayerSource carries an explicit tile_order (zyx|zxy) and per-layer file_extension.
decisions.rationale: NASA Trek WMTS serves {z}/{row=y}/{col=x} (verified) while our result XYZ tiles are {z}/{x}/{y}; and Trek products differ in format (jpeg vs png) per product (confirmed by data-access). Encoding both removes client guesswork.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Assuming a single global tile order/extension (would 404 half the layers).

risks.risk: NASA Trek product ids and tile format vary per product (jpeg vs png), and guessed ids (MOLA-DEM, THEMIS) 404 — a wrong id/extension yields blank layers.
risks.mitigation: LayerSource carries explicit product-derived url_template + per-layer file_extension + tile_order; LayerAvailability records a probed sample tile (status/http_status/checked_at). Only VERIFIED products ship enabled; others start availability=unconfirmed. Confirm ids via the Trek searchItems catalog API (verified by data-access).

risks.risk: CRISM MTRDR cubes are large; bulk download violates the 'API/service only, tiny bundles' constraint and would break offline CI.
risks.mitigation: Contract is storage/source agnostic: Observation.source_url points at the ODE service; the engine fetches on demand; ship a tiny synthetic/sample COG + one reference spectrum as fixtures so the pipeline and tiles render offline in CI.

risks.risk: Pydantic<->TS<->OpenAPI could drift over time.
risks.mitigation: OpenAPI is generated from Pydantic (contracts/gen_openapi.py); TS is tsc --strict checked; CONTRACT_VERSION + enums.json are the shared pin; add a CI step asserting the live /openapi.json matches contracts/openapi.yaml.

risks.risk: GeoJSON spec mandates WGS84, but coordinates are Mars IAU 2000 — naive GIS tooling may misinterpret them.
risks.mitigation: crs block in enums.json documents the datum/ellipsoid; bounds/bbox/footprint are plain degrees; frontend configures a Mars ellipsoid; no Earth reprojection is ever applied.

risks.risk: A detection could be presented as a confirmed mineral deposit (explicitly forbidden).
risks.mitigation: caveat is a REQUIRED field on AnalysisResult, SummaryStats, Legend and Provenance, sourced from the single CANDIDATE_MATCH_CAVEAT constant; the type system makes a caveat-less result unrepresentable.

risks.risk: extra=forbid rejects any additive field, which can break clients on an uncoordinated change.
risks.mitigation: Treat the contract as versioned: additive changes bump CONTRACT_VERSION and land in all three artifacts together; forbid is what forces that coordination rather than silent divergence.

risks.risk: Observation id casing/format differs across providers (ODE returns lowercase).
risks.mitigation: id is an opaque string stored exactly as the provider returns it; lookups are case-sensitive and clients use ids verbatim from list responses.

verified_facts: NASA Trek basemap tiles reachable (HTTP 200 image/jpeg): Mars_Viking_MDIM21_ClrMosaic_global_232m and Mars_MGS_MOLA_ClrShade_merge_global_463m at z0 1/0/0; guessed ids Mars_MGS_MOLA_DEM_mosaic_global_463m and three THEMIS id variants all 404 (so DEM/THEMIS must be resolved via the Trek catalog API).

Trek tile order is {z}/{row=y}/{col=x} (north-origin): at z4 the Nili Fossae tile 4/6/22 (row/col) returns 200 while swapped 4/22/6 returns 404 — confirms tile_order=zyx, geographic grid, 2 cols x 1 row at z0. Encoded in LayerSource.tile_order and contracts/enums.json.
